releases.name: OpenCode plugin 0.1.4
releases.body:
OpenCode plugin **0.1.4** ships the latest master changes: explicit scope policy across review, validation, application and resume, plus visible scope tags in Markdown and HTML review reports.

Set the exact plugin pin in your OpenCode config and restart while online:

```json
{ "plugin": ["opencode-multi-llm@0.1.4"] }
```

Tested host: **OpenCode 1.19.5 on Linux**. macOS and Windows remain untested on the npm installation route. Keep the other entries and settings in your existing config. Project `.multi-llm/providers.yaml` stays in place; this release needs no provider-config migration. Users switching from the file-command route should remove the old file command before enabling the npm plugin to avoid duplicate commands.

All nine canonical fresh-registry criteria passed: exact package integrity and tree, manifest version, installed command, actual payload execution, cold dependency installation, offline operation with network cut, same-pin restart, and a real **0.1.3 → 0.1.4** upgrade executing the new payload. No paid model requests were used.

Immutable tag source: `89fea1893ec332fc5462c5b95ee712404a898d32`. Accepted npm provenance identifies certified publishing source `8d605c9b9d74ba6b4580081838296126212d8802` on `refs/heads/master`, repository `beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin`, workflow `.github/workflows/publish-opencode-plugin.yml`. Its rebuilt package digest exactly equals the independently gated tag: `bcdf5f4fb5f402dad25402603e49497180050acdd1d07f59ba6ea5a51d5ca905`.

Registry integrity:

```text
sha512-qajLxl8eSG2qzkmwEDYgW301/xd4rN+CPq59Al3STbc0cjtH1A5rtY69S3sVr9NC07EBi0FEV762zsDrjDYqcQ==
```

All four required PR and master CI checks and both local/tag release gates passed. Publish: [successful OIDC workflow](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/actions/runs/41278049174).

Attached evidence: `20261101T004126Z-opencode-release-gate.json`, `20261101T061412Z-opencode-release-network-check.json` (also committed under `skills/multi-llm/tests/container/records/`), `certified-source-equivalence.json`, and `npm-provenance-verification.json`.

releases.name: Codex plugin 0.1.4
releases.body:
Codex plugin **0.1.4** ships the latest master changes: explicit scope policy across review, validation, application and resume, plus visible scope tags in Markdown and HTML review reports.

Upgrade an existing marketplace installation:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace upgrade beastlabai
codex plugin add multi-llm@beastlabai
```

For a new installation, first add the marketplace:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin --ref release \
  --sparse .agents --sparse packaging/codex
codex plugin add multi-llm@beastlabai
```

Start a new Codex session. Existing project provider configuration stays in place. Tag-pinned users should select `codex-v0.1.4`.

Verified source: `89fea1893ec332fc5462c5b95ee712404a898d32`. All four PR and master CI checks passed. The full local gate passed 17 rows on Codex 0.163.0, 10 on minimum 0.159.2, and 10 on latest 0.166.0. The upstream validator is absent; repository layout rules and actual Codex ingestion passed.

Fresh public tag and promoted-release installs passed all six criteria, with all 218 files matching the tag. A real public-release 0.1.3 → 0.1.4 marketplace upgrade executed the new MCP payload; same-version refresh preserved its bytes. No paid model requests were used.

Evidence: attached canonical `20261101T031024Z-codex-release-network-check.json` (also committed under `skills/multi-llm/tests/container/records/`) and sanitized `codex-public-verification.json`. Promotion: [successful workflow](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/actions/runs/41278047801).

releases.name: OpenCode plugin 0.1.3
releases.body:
The OpenCode Multi-LLM plugin now includes the current master runtime, including commit-range review and guarded fix workflows, sharper review prompts, and detached-log fixes. Shared version: 0.1.3.

Requires OpenCode 1.19.5 or newer and uv on PATH. Change your exact plugin pin and restart OpenCode:

```json
{ "plugin": ["opencode-multi-llm@0.1.3"] }
```

Confirm it loaded with `opencode debug config` and check that `command["multi-llm"]` exists. Existing provider configuration is preserved. File-route users should first run `uninstall-host opencode` from their original installation to remove its command shim.

The full local gate passed rows 1–9 and 5b on OpenCode 1.19.5, including all five installed-package container scenarios. Release source: `c9ae61b027a9e7bac4db216353495077f9c1d6f2`. [Committed gate record](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/blob/master/skills/multi-llm/tests/container/records/20261030T155243Z-opencode-release-gate.json). The publisher preserves GitHub-certified source metadata and requires its rebuilt package digest to equal the independently gated release tag. The dispatch-source rebuild at `cfe445b4543b733b9754df807f1e7c224fb15de7` matches that digest exactly. The OIDC publication succeeded with npm 11.5.1 and Node 22.23.4. Its accepted provenance identifies the correct repository, `.github/workflows/publish-opencode-plugin.yml`, and certified dispatch source `cfe445b4543b733b9754df807f1e7c224fb15de7`; the published subject digest matches the registry package. [Publishing run](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/actions/runs/41129206642).

A fresh stock-container install passed all nine later-release criteria, including exact installed-tree equality with the tag, first-use dependencies, offline operation with the network cut, restart, and an actual upgrade from 0.1.1 executing the new payload. [Committed registry install/upgrade proof](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/blob/master/skills/multi-llm/tests/container/records/20261030T214755Z-opencode-release-network-check.json).

Integrity: `sha512-b4rfpMp/eLCeYMx506jEyRbCIXzgfg9DKChejXIyxHAFMDUZH/01Jw4wWkHiOLdqNDojfV08K16/gaybJQxpYg==`.

The gate record, registry proof, source-equivalence proof, and provenance verification are attached. Raw supporting logs remain local because they contain machine-specific paths. All package and install checks used local stubs; no paid model calls were made.

releases.name: Codex plugin 0.1.3
releases.body:
The Multi-LLM Codex plugin now includes the current master runtime: commit-range review and guarded fix workflows, sharper review prompts, detached-log fixes, Windows process cleanup fixes, and the BeastLab composer icon. Shared version: 0.1.3.

Upgrade:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace upgrade beastlabai
codex plugin add multi-llm@beastlabai
# Start a new Codex session.
```

Requirements: Codex >=0.159.2, python3 >=3.9, and uv on PATH. Provider configuration is preserved; review the current defaults before choosing to regenerate it. The full gate passed on Codex 0.159.2 (10 checks), 0.163.0 (17 checks), and 0.166.0 (10 checks). A fresh stock container installed the public tag with Codex 0.166.0: all six criteria passed, and all 213 installed files matched the tag before first use. The upstream validator is absent; package layout is verified by repository rules and Codex ingestion.

Release source: `c9ae61b027a9e7bac4db216353495077f9c1d6f2`. [Committed install proof](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/blob/master/skills/multi-llm/tests/container/records/20261030T181607Z-codex-release-network-check.json). All release gates and install probes use no paid model calls.

To adopt the updated default model roster, back up your custom `.multi-llm/providers.yaml` and reinitialize with `--init --force`; existing custom configuration is otherwise preserved.

After promotion, the documented `--ref release` install was verified in another fresh stock container: all six criteria pass. `marketplace upgrade` plus `plugin add` preserved the exact 213-file payload and release commit. Both install records are attached.

releases.name: OpenCode plugin 0.1.1
releases.body:
First release of **`opencode-multi-llm`**, the multi-llm workflow inside OpenCode, installed from npm. multi-llm runs plan reviews, task generation, implementation and code review across several LLM CLIs. The package adds a `/multi-llm` command and a model-callable `multi_llm` tool.

## Install

Add the exact pin to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, then restart OpenCode:

```json
{ "plugin": ["opencode-multi-llm@0.1.1"] }
```

Check that it loaded. Every failure on this route is silent: the entry stays listed and nothing reports an error.

```bash
opencode debug config | jq '.command["multi-llm"] != null'   # true = loaded
```

Then, once per repository, run `/multi-llm --init`. It writes `<git-root>/.multi-llm/providers.yaml`, where you pick your providers and models. After that, run a workflow: `/multi-llm plans/my-feature.md`. Headless, the command is `opencode run --command multi-llm -- "plans/my-feature.md"`.

- **Requirements:** opencode **1.19.4 or newer**, enforced through `engines` (an older opencode refuses the package with a compatibility error), and `uv` on `PATH`, which supplies Python itself.
- **First run:** the first start downloads the package, and the first `/multi-llm` builds its Python environment (`pyyaml` alone). Both need the network.
- **Always pin.** OpenCode caches a plugin under the exact string in `plugin`, so an unpinned name or a range resolves once and never updates. To upgrade, change the pin and restart.

Full instructions: [README §1.3](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/blob/master/README.md#13-opencode) and [docs/hosts.md](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/blob/master/docs/hosts.md#opencode-npm-route). The latter covers troubleshooting, uninstall and local builds.

## Coming from the file route

If you installed with `install-host opencode`, remove that command file from the checkout or plugin install you ran it from, then add the pin above:

```bash
uv run --frozen --no-dev --project "$SKILL" -- python "$SKILL/multi_llm.py" uninstall-host opencode --dry-run   # lists the files
uv run --frozen --no-dev --project "$SKILL" -- python "$SKILL/multi_llm.py" uninstall-host opencode
```

A leftover file does no harm, because the package's command replaces it at startup. `install-host opencode --check` reports `BOTH routes` until it's removed.

## What was checked

- **The full local release gate** (`make opencode-package-check`) on `f4f024c7`: rows 1–9 and 5b pass. That includes:
  - a clean install of the exact tarball by opencode 1.19.4, in a committed project and in a project with no commits;
  - five container scenarios run through the installed package with stub models and no credentials: `init`/`status`, detached launch, supervision, completion and cancellation;
  - registry absence immediately before the upload.

  Record: [`skills/multi-llm/tests/container/records/20261026T125425Z-opencode-release-gate.json`](https://github.com/beastlabai/multi-llm-plugin/blob/master/skills/multi-llm/tests/container/records/20261026T125425Z-opencode-release-gate.json).
- **CI on the release commit:** the test suite on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows, and the package job, all green.
- **The upload is the gated tarball itself** (`npm publish <tarball> --ignore-scripts`). The registry serves integrity `sha512-XjxHpcySLlsWfUQdlApgEM82ojLfJg1SD9pkAbkGPw5pv0j0+29iQJtxGb9vEQLaQNZw8VJMSs+CSpDfswCFoQ==`, identical to the gated one.
- **Installed as a user would,** from registry.npmjs.org, into a fresh stock `node:22-bookworm-slim` container: opencode 1.19.4, uv 0.13.5, empty caches, no checkout of this repository, and a new project made with a plain `git init`. All eight first-release criteria pass:

  - the installed manifest says 0.1.1;
